subject: TTFT framing & chunk cadence — follow-up and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Wilson <ava@finverse.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT framing & chunk cadence — post-demo notes

Thanks for the demo earlier, Ava — good discussion. Quick recap and a handful of concrete asks so engineering can size the pilot: 

What we covered / targets you mentioned:
- TTFT target: 80–120 ms p95 for user-facing chat upsell flows (mobile web + iOS).
- Typical request profile: prompt ~150–220 tokens, model response ~150–300 tokens (will confirm averages below).
- Concurrency expectation: steady 150–200 concurrent users; spikes up to ~400 during batch syncs/market events.
- Streaming preference: you said WebSocket works better for your client; SSE could be acceptable for dashboard flows.
- Chunk cadence: you prefer frequent small chunks (roughly 1–3 chunk/sec) to keep UI progressive.

As next steps from Redwood side:
1) Can you confirm average and 95th token lengths for both prompts and responses (we need median & p95).
2) If you can share a short production sample (anonymized) or a tokenization map, that will help us choose kv-cache and batching params.
3) We'll propose a 2-week pilot (performance-run) with a perf-probe you can run on your side. Attached is an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a lightweight perf probe script we typically use.

If the numbers above look right, I'll draft the pilot scope + success criteria and loop in our infra lead (Marcus) to schedule a 30–45m tech sync.

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Ava Wilson <ava@finverse.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Finverse Engineering Team <eng-team@finverse.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT framing & chunk cadence — post-demo notes

Thanks Sergio — that recap is accurate. Quick answers while I pull the tokenized samples: 
- Median prompt: 180 tokens; p95 prompt: 320 tokens.
- Median response: 210 tokens; p95 response: 420 tokens.
- Concurrency: baseline 150–200; traffic generator shows spikes to 420–450 in market simulations.
- Streaming: primary client uses WebSocket. Dashboards prefer SSE for simplicity, but we can accept either.

I'll share a sanitized sample set and a link to our internal performance spreadsheet by end of day. We're keen on the 2-week pilot — please send the MAP and pilot success metrics and we'll route NDA/redlines internally.

—Ava
Ava Wilson
Head of Product — Finverse AI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Wilson <ava@finverse.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT framing & chunk cadence — post-demo notes

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Ava. A few engineering questions to make the pilot deterministic: 

1) Tokenization & prompt shapes- Do the prompts include long system instructions or mostly user messages? If system tokens are heavy (>50 tokens) that changes cache warmup.
2) Max sequence length — what should we assume for internal safety checks & kv cache sizing (max total tokens input+output)?
3) Client behavior — do clients maintain a persistent session socket per user or do they create short-lived sockets per request? This affects connection scaling (we can multiplex).
4) Streaming preference — WebSocket default is fine; for the pilot we'd like to exercise SSE as fallback to validate chunk cadence. Can you confirm if dashboard flows can tolerate slightly larger chunks (e.g., 100–200 token chunks every 500–750 ms)?

Pilot-technical proposal (short):
- Probe run: 48h synthetic run + 2 weekdays of live ramp. We'll measure TTFT p50/p95, end-to-end token throughput, and memory/kv-cache hit rates.
- Load profile: steady 200 concurrency with scheduled spikes to 450 for 10–20m windows; repeat 6x per day during spike windows.
- Metrics: TTFT p50/p95, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, token-level batching stats, and chunk-delivery latency distribution.

I've attached a tiny perf-probe.sh you can run inside your environment (no secret keys). If you can run that against our staging endpoint and attach the raw CSV, we'll pick sensible batching/quantization and a candidate model variant.

Tagging Neha to own the pilot timeline and SLO definitions with you, Ava.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ava Wilson <ava@finverse.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Finverse Engineering Team <eng-team@finverse.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT framing & chunk cadence — post-demo notes

Marcus — answers below and attaching the sample logs you requested (sanitized).

1) Prompts: most conversations include a 30–60 token system instruction + user history (avg 2–3 prior messages). So system overhead ~45 tokens typical.
2) Max sequence length: target safe limit 1024 tokens (we rarely exceed this, but spike scenarios can push close).
3) Client sockets: mobile clients maintain a persistent socket while the chat session is active (~2–10 minutes). Web clients often open a socket per conversation tab.
4) Chunk cadence: dashboards can accept ~200 token chunks every 500–800 ms; real-time chat wants smaller chunks every ~300–500 ms. WebSocket preferred for chat.

Attached: finverse-sample-logs.txt (sanitized). We can run your perf-probe on our staging this week — scheduled window Thursday morning.

Also: here's the DocuSign link for the pilot NDA: https://app.docusign.com/invite?doc=finverse-pilot-nda. We'll push internally for quick approval but pinging procurement could shave a day.

Thanks — sending the sample sheet now.
—Ava
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Wilson <ava@finverse.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT framing & chunk cadence — follow-up & pilot scheduling

Perfect — thanks for the details and the sample logs, Ava. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) We'll formalize the pilot scope today (objective: demonstrate sustained TTFT p95 <= 120 ms under your steady/peak profile). I'll add a secondary goal for chunk cadence: chat p95 chunk arrival <= 500 ms, dashboard chunk cadence <= 800 ms.
2) Marcus & Neha will schedule a 45m tech sync for this Thursday 10/22 at 10:30am PT to review probe results and wire up the staging endpoint.
3) Please sign the pilot NDA (link you provided); once countersigned we'll spin a dedicated staging endpoint and share per-route traces.
4) Deliverables for the pilot: perf CSVs, MAP signoff, short rollback/runbook, and a final go/no-go decision at the end of the 2 week window.

I've added the HubSpot deal (RDW-7821) and Drive link to the related_links field for internal tracking. Marcus — can you confirm which model variant you'd like us to stage (quantized 8-bit candidate + baseline fp16) so Finverse can simulate both?

Ava — ideally we'll start the probe on Thu morning as you suggested and then do the live spike windows next Mon/Tue to match your market event cadence.

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

On Thu, Oct 22 at 10:30am PT — tentative tech sync (calendar invite to follow).
